answer: Hand every agent one unique 10 GB encrypted shard to guard, drawn from the ocean of network data and locked under its own cipher key. Each epoch, five random spot-checks demand a Merkle proof for a random slice; a real custodian answers in seconds, while a puppet farm must fetch or rebuild the slice first. Miss twice and the agent loses its 100-token bond and its seat. The shard rests in glacier-cold storage, cheap to keep yet ruinous to fake at scale: 1,000 puppets need 10 TB of disk plus 400 setup hours, about $9,500 a month. A fisherman mends one net and knows every knot by feel.
